holdings.thesis: HOLD: sixth consecutive stop-loss review (-40.3% vs. cost basis, price ~$161.49, recovering from ~$150 earlier in the week). No new company-specific negative catalyst since 9/14 -- Credo is presenting at the AI Infra Summit 2026 (Santa Clara, 9/15-17), showcasing 1.6T optical interconnects; Stifel flagged a prospective $600M optical ramp opportunity across multiple hyperscalers, and sell-side remains unanimously bullish (consensus PT ~$281, BofA Buy $275, Evercore Buy $292). FY27 guidance still implies 85%+ revenue growth. Position is already a de-risked ~5.3% stub after three prior trims -- holding.

HOLD: thesis intact and reinforced. A 9/16 report describes Duolingo folding former "Max" AI features (video calls, mistake-explanations) directly into the base Super tier as AI inference costs fall -- consistent with the 9/14 Motley Fool framing of the shift away from the legacy paid tier as a positive long-term monetization move, and with CEO von Ahn's 100M-DAU-by-2028 commentary from the 9/9 Citi conference. The persistent earnings-decline flag continues to reflect deliberate AI-feature reinvestment, not demand weakness. Position ~14.75% of portfolio, just under the 15% cap -- hold, don't add; any further appreciation may force a mechanical trim on sizing alone.

HOLD: seventh consecutive stop-loss review (-30.1% vs. cost basis, price ~$55.41). Director Louise Forlenza sold another ~10,000 shares on 9/14 (Form 4 filed 9/15, ~$535K), but this continues the same recurring diversification-style selling pattern already reviewed (prior tranches $1.7M/$2.67M/$1.8M), not a new escalation. CEO succession (Singhal to CEO, Abuhoff to Executive Chairman effective 9/30) remains on track with no reported disruption; 58% YoY revenue growth and 40%+ FY guidance reaffirmed and unchanged. Holding the remaining ~1.4% stub through the transition.

TRIMMED 30% today: this was the first-ever stop-loss breach for VRT (-25.9% vs. cost basis at review time, price ~$239.41), and unlike CRDO/INOD's chronic pattern this looked like a fresh crossing driven almost entirely by Monday's broad AI-sentiment selloff amplified by Vertiv's ~2x beta -- shares were already recovering (~$234 on 9/15 toward ~$240+ on 9/16). No earnings miss, guidance cut, or litigation; Q2 organic-growth guidance was actually raised (20-22% CAGR through 2030), and sell-side remains heavily bullish (83% buy-rated, ~$341 avg PT, GLJ upgraded to Buy $381). But the 9/9 UtilityInnovation Group acquisition ($1.45B plus up to $1.15B earnout, ~13x 2027 EBITDA) still has undisclosed target financials, and the Massachusetts data-center permitting order remains an overhang -- combined with the high beta, that's less-diversifiable risk into a choppy AI-infra tape. Trimmed 30% (0.5772 sh) to de-risk given the fresh breach, keeping the bulk of the position since there is no thesis-breaking catalyst.

HOLD: no negative catalyst; incremental positives since 9/14 -- Alphabet closed its ~$1.5B acquisition of AI-coding startup Mechanize (DeepMind talent/tech tuck-in), and Waymo announced a planned Munich robotaxi launch by end-2027. Position ~15.5%, a touch over the nominal 15% target but within the trim tolerance band -- watch for sizing drift, no action needed today.

HOLD: one new item to monitor, not thesis-breaking -- CNBC/Insurance Journal (9/15-16) reported AWS still cannot restore its Bahrain data center and one UAE availability zone, with the Bahrain infrastructure damage (from March Iran-related strikes) possibly unrecoverable and no update expected before early 2027. This is a regional reliability/reputational issue, not a broad US AWS outage; no revenue/customer-impact disclosure yet. Thesis otherwise intact -- watch for a follow-up disclosure.

HOLD: mildly positive update -- Texas regulators approved ExxonMobil's plan to inject ~53M metric tons of CO2 as part of its $5B carbon capture project (9/15); a Pioneer debt tender offer is routine. Thesis (strong Q2 earnings, Angola Block 15 discovery) unchanged.

HOLD: Affirm execs (Risk/Capital Markets/IR, not CEO/CFO) presented at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference on 9/15, reiterating the existing growth story -- 36% GMV growth, Affirm Card scaling, the 5-year Amazon renewal -- with no new guidance surprises. Thesis intact.

HOLD: no material news -- the only new item is a routine, pre-scheduled Rule 10b5-1 insider sale by the Chief Product Officer (~$2.8M, reported 9/16), not a signal. AI-observability demand thesis unchanged.

HOLD: no material news yet -- Lilly announced (9/15) it will present new cardiometabolic data (orforglipron/Foundayo, retatrutide, eloraTZP) at EASD 2026 in Milan, an upcoming catalyst to watch rather than new data itself. Obesity-franchise/donanemab thesis intact.

HOLD, flagging a new litigation risk: Citizens Bank filed a federal lawsuit (filed ~9/10, widely reported 9/15) in Connecticut alleging SoFi orchestrated poaching of ~30 mortgage loan officers and trade-secret misuse, including a RICO claim tied to SoFi's home-loan business. This is a reputational/legal overhang on the mortgage business, not an immediate financial hit or a break of the core digital-bank/fintech thesis -- holding, monitoring for developments.

HOLD, flagging sentiment risk: shares extended a pullback (~4% around 9/14-16) on renewed AI-data-center-capex-slowdown sentiment (media reports questioning hyperscaler capex), which reads directly against the Power & Energy segment's AI-genset/turbine growth driver. No earnings, guidance, or contract news; $72B backlog and core industrial thesis unchanged. Worth watching given the direct read-through to the thesis, but not thesis-breaking today.

HOLD: no material news since 9/14 -- a CEO share sale reported 9/16 was a tax-related Rule 10b5-1 vesting transaction, not a signal. Thesis (raised FY26 revenue guidance post-SkyWater, quantum-computing pure-play) unchanged. Holding the modest ~2.2% position.

HOLD: no company-specific news since 9/14; shares dipped ~3% on 9/15 on general rate-sensitivity/insider-selling-overhang sentiment rather than any new headline. Thesis (incoming-CEO Paul Gu insider purchase, AI-underwriting) intact.

HOLD: no new headlines since the 9/9 items already reflected in thesis (Q1 FY27 beat, $1.5B backlog, LOCUST/Titan contract wins). Defense/drone thesis intact and strengthening (+11.1% vs. cost basis).

BUY: AST SpaceMobile sourced from the 9/8 weekly theme screen (direct-to-cell satellite connectivity). Shifting from proof-of-concept to commercial activation: BlueBird 11-13 satellites deployed, a new New Zealand gateway opened, deepening integration tests with Vodafone/Orange/Telefonica/Deutsche Telekom via a gateway JV, and US Mobile preparing a direct-to-cell launch. 2026 revenue guided to $150-200M off a near-zero base (drove the screen's outsized revenue-growth score), backed by a $1.3B backlog and over $3.7B cash on hand -- funds the capital-intensive buildout without near-term dilution risk. Known risk: execution on an expensive, tightly-timed deployment (targets imply ~165%/yr revenue growth through 2029); stock is down modestly on the mixed reaction to the BlueBird/US Mobile news despite the bull case being intact per sell-side (~$78 fair-value estimate vs. ~$59 entry). Not opportunity-tier (market cap ~$23B). Sized to $79 (~2.0% of portfolio), the remaining room in the Technology sector cap (already ~28% of portfolio before this buy) rather than a full-size position -- funded by today's VRT trim proceeds.
